title: Cross-environment keycache index corruption and GPU OOMs — emergency runtime hotpatch and staged rollout
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary: Over the last 72 hours we received three escalations (two Hosted, one Dedicated) reporting sudden GPU OOMs coinciding with degraded tail-latency and sustained memory usage growth on long-running sessions. Investigation shows correlated increases in keycache journal fragmentation and repeated key index resyncs; in several cases stale index entries prevented proper eviction and caused the GPU allocator to stall and leak session handles. The bug appears across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments with different manifestation thresholds due to divergent workload mixes and memory pressure profiles.

Root cause hypothesis: A race in the keycache journal compaction path where concurrent eviction + snapshot merge can leave dangling index pointers during low-frequency tombstone reconciliation. When the serving runtime later attempts to reclaim arenas, the allocator hits inconsistent free lists and fails to compact, causing persistent fragmentation that leads to runaway GPU reservation for some sessions and eventual OOM. Secondary factor: long-tail autoregressive requests with large KV footprints avoid typical short-circuit evictions, amplifying the leak.

Impact: Several customer endpoints experienced request failures and degraded throughput. One Dedicated customer reported sustained service degradation requiring traffic migration. Hosted incidents affected multiple tenants with transient token throttles and increased retries.

Goal: Ship a minimal, low-risk runtime hotpatch that: 1) prevents the dangling pointer state by adding linearized journal merge fencing, 2) tightens eviction heuristics under fragmentation, and 3) provides an emergency runtime-level emergency reclaim path to break allocator stalls. Roll out canary -> regional -> global with rollback plan and customer communication.

Scope of work: triage live incidents, implement hotpatch, unit/integration tests for the journal merge, synthetic stress tests against long-tail session traces, canary rollout to non-prod then one low-risk region, upgrade procedure for Dedicated/Private nodes, customer-facing postmortem and KB article, and longer-term follow-ups for allocator defragmentation improvements.
acceptance_criteria: Hotpatch merged and CI green for unit + integration tests covering concurrent journal compaction scenarios
Canary rollout to eu-west-1 and staging with 48h monitoring showing no OOM regressions on historical replay traces
Memory fragmentation metrics (arena free-percentiles) improve by at least 20% on replay workload within 24h of rollout
Customer-reported incidents resolve for impacted tenants and affected Dedicated customer confirms restored baseline throughput
Rollback validated and automated; runtime-2.4.1-hotfix tagged and release notes published
updates: 2026-03-10 — Initial triage: identified correlation between journal compaction timestamp spikes and first OOM at 04:12 UTC; created ENG-424242 and alerted SRE on-call
2026-03-11 — Reproduced leak locally using replay of hosted-session trace; added instrumentation for journal op ordering and allocator free-list integrity checks
2026-03-12 — Implemented fenced journal merge proof-of-concept; ran stress test (48h) on staging with no additional leaks observed
2026-03-13 — PR opened for hotpatch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1892 (contains patch + new unit tests)

2026-03-14 — Canary rollout plan approved by SRE and Product; selected eu-west-1 (low-risk) and a dedicated customer test node; monitoring dashboards created: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/mem-frag-ENG-424242
2026-03-15 — Canary started (10% traffic) against eu-west-1; early signals: allocator stall metrics down 35% vs baseline; no OOMs in first 12h. Continuing 48h watch before broader rollout
communication_plan: Notify impacted customers with current mitigation steps and ETA for hotpatch (support template sent)
Publish status update in customer portal after canary completes (or earlier if regression observed)
Schedule postmortem with SRE/PM/EM and affected customer success managers within 72h of full rollback or complete rollout
